task_row_model.query: What were the inclusion criteria and the primary endpoint for the multicenter phase II trial of drug X?

documents.content: Background: The multicenter phase II study evaluated drug X in advanced non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Eligibility required adult patients (age ≥18) with ECOG performance status 0–1 and histologically confirmed advanced NSCLC harboring an activating EGFR mutation. The protocol specified the primary efficacy measure as objective response rate (ORR) assessed at 12 weeks. Methods section referenced RECIST v1.1 for response assessment. A brief historical note about EGFR pathway discovery was included as context for the drug’s mechanism, but no other endpoints were primary.
documents.reasoning_trace: Contains age ≥18, ECOG 0–1, histologically confirmed advanced NSCLC with activating EGFR mutation; states primary endpoint = ORR assessed at 12 weeks and references RECIST v1.1.

documents.content: A news-style report summarized enrollment criteria for the trial: patients needed measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 and documented progression after prior platinum-based chemotherapy. The piece noted the study ran at sites across the US and Europe and quoted investigators about enrollment speed; it also cited unrelated regional incidence statistics and an anecdotal case study of a patient treated off-protocol, which are not part of eligibility criteria.
documents.reasoning_trace: Provides measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 and requirement of progression after platinum-based chemotherapy; other material is contextual/news noise.

documents.content: Protocol memo (informal): Response assessments were to be centrally adjudicated — all investigator-reported responses required confirmation by independent radiology review according to RECIST v1.1 criteria. The memo reiterated the 12-week assessment window for the primary outcome and listed standard exclusion items (prior investigational EGFR inhibitors, uncontrolled brain metastases). There was speculative commentary about exploratory biomarker analyses, but the memo focused on timing and confirmation procedures for the ORR primary endpoint.
documents.reasoning_trace: Confirms that ORR at 12 weeks must be confirmed by independent radiology review per RECIST v1.1; mentions timing and confirmation procedure relevant to the primary endpoint.

documents.content: Reference entry: Objective response rate (ORR) is commonly used in oncology trials and denotes the proportion of patients with partial or complete response by predefined criteria; ECOG performance status ranges from 0 (fully active) to 5. The entry provided definitional boilerplate about RECIST versions and speculative discussion about surrogate endpoints in oncology, plus unrelated historical trial summaries and some redundant restatements of definitions.
documents.reasoning_trace: General definitions of ORR and ECOG provided as background; contains no trial-specific inclusion criteria beyond definitional boilerplate and is mainly noise.

task_row_model.golden_answer: Inclusion criteria: adults (≥18) with ECOG performance status 0–1, histologically confirmed advanced NSCLC with an activating EGFR mutation, measurable disease per RECIST v1.1, and documented progression after platinum‑based chemotherapy. Primary endpoint: objective response rate (ORR) at 12 weeks per RECIST v1.1, confirmed by independent radiology review.
